reason: No prior evidence is cited to support any of the key premises; the hypothesis relies entirely on general mechanistic reasoning without specific experimental or computational backing.
premises: Rapid quenching freezes a high density of defects, grain boundaries, and lattice strains in HEA nanoparticles.
Slow cooling allows defect annealing and atomic rearrangement toward equilibrium, reducing defect densities.
Defects, grain boundaries, and lattice strains serve as catalytic active sites.
Higher defect density correlates with enhanced catalytic performance (e.g., higher turnover frequency).
These relationships hold for noble metal HEA nanoparticles synthesized at ~500°C under inert atmosphere.
